prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished desktop website design comp, 1536x1024 landscape: a real web layout, edge to edge, no device frame, no browser chrome.

The FIRST attached image is the approved look and feel for this page: match its header, type, spacing, white cards, canary-yellow buttons and highlights, and above all its premium matte isometric miniature desk (pale wood desktop, green blotter, a small canary, an open brass birdcage, soft studio daylight, one contact shadow). The other attached images are the same site's built homepage: they confirm the header (script wordmark "Birdcar" at left; nav "How I work", "Selected work", "Writing" and a canary-yellow pill "Book a free Walkthrough →"), the pale daylight ground #edf3f0, near-black ink #0b141a, the heavy tight grotesk (Mona Sans) for all text, white pill tags, and canary yellow #f7c848 only on actions and highlights. Do NOT copy any reference's content beyond that style; do not paint invented words on props (no text on notebooks, book spines, or signs).

This page is "The Walkthrough": the booking page for a free, pitch-free, roughly one-hour conversation with Nick (Birdcar), a systems engineer who builds tools for established service businesses. Within three business days the visitor gets a written report they keep: what's happening, what I recommend, and where I'd start. New requirement for this page: the visitor qualifies themselves before reaching the calendar. The fit check uses these exact lines: "You have customers and people doing the work." / "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." / "I can talk to the people who do it." and the honest disqualifier "If I can't talk to the people doing the work, I'm not the right fit."

STRUCTURE, in reading order (a sticky desk beside the questions: the page scrolls through the fit questions on the left while the desk and its calendar stay pinned on the right). Show the page scrolled partway down, just past the opening, so the pinned relationship is visible:
1. Header, about 80px, as the reference.
2. LEFT column (x 80 to 700), scrolling content: at the top, the tail of the opening, the headline about 52px "An hour on the work. A report you can use." and one line "In a free Walkthrough, you spend about an hour showing me the work that's giving you trouble." Then the fit questions as large stacked blocks separated by hairlines, each with a round check circle at its left: block 1 heading about 30px "You have customers and people doing the work." with one muted sentence "The operational problem matters more than the industry." (its check circle filled ink). Block 2 heading "One process takes too much chasing, copying, or remembering." with "You don't need to diagnose it first. Bring one example." (check filled). Block 3 heading "I can talk to the people who do it." with "If that isn't possible, I'm not the right fit." (check circle empty, outlined).
3. RIGHT column (x 760 to 1460, y 100 to 940), pinned: the miniature desk from the reference with the white calendar card standing on it, showing "The Walkthrough", "About 60 minutes · Video call or in person", a month grid "October 2026" with available dates ringed, a column of times and a canary-yellow "Book this time →" button. At the top of the calendar card, a slim white pill row reads "2 of 3 checked" with three small dots, two filled canary yellow. The canary perches on the card's corner; the open brass birdcage at the right.

ART DIRECTION: one dominant move, the pinned desk; the left column is calm, large, readable type. Premium, adult, precise. Not cute. No purple, no gradient orbs, no robots, no AI imagery, no stock photos, no prices, no fake metrics, no testimonials. Preserve all quoted words exactly. Treat it as a finished, shippable website.
